materials.rationale: The main wall field on every elevation is smooth, regular RECTANGULAR-coursed brick — uniform mortar lines, flat faces. This is the cool-grey structural body; kept distinct from the rougher cobblestone corners.

The four corner pilasters (and the band running under the eave) show a visibly ROUGH, rounded, irregular cobble grain — bumpy, non-coursed — against the smooth stone-brick field. Near-tone grey but a DIFFERENT material; must not collapse into stone_bricks.
The steep gable slope reads as dark, tight, cool-grey tiling — markedly darker than the walls so the roof recedes and the gable reads as silhouette. Distinct dark tone, not the lighter wall stone.

A chunky 1-block band of warm dark-brown TIMBER with visible log grain rings the arched gate — the single warm note against the all-grey stone. Distinct material (wood, not stone) framing the opening.

Inside the timber arch the recessed door/passage fill is the same warm dark wood but reads as flat sawn boards rather than the round log frame — kept as a distinct opening fill (planks) vs the log voussoir.
